central_question: As of December 31, 2027, what will be the state of the Russia-Ukraine war on the continuum from full-scale active war through reduced-intensity attrition, frozen conflict/de facto ceasefire, formal armistice, to comprehensive peace settlement — including territory held and strike tempo — and what are its economic, geopolitical and market implications?

situation_brief.current_situation: As of late October 2026 Russia holds about 45,196 square miles (~19% of Ukraine) including Crimea and pre-2022 Donbas, but has net-lost ground since September 1, 2026, with ISW judging its Donetsk offensive 'operationally defeated'. Strike tempo remains high (6,732 Shahed-type UAVs in September 2026). After Putin's ninth in-person meeting with US envoy Steve Witkoff on October 21, 2026, the Kremlin agreed to resume trilateral technical-level talks, possibly in Abu Dhabi, on or after November 10, 2026, focused on post-war security guarantees.
situation_brief.context: The war is in its fifth year. Baseline prices embed a geopolitical premium: Brent at 102.0181 USD/bbl (Sept 2026) versus 67.6091 a year earlier; TTF Nov26 at 88.430 EUR/MWh (Oct 22, 2026). Russia's draft 2027 budget allocates 17.1 trillion roubles to defence; Ukraine faces a €70 billion 2027 financing gap with the EU providing 80% of external aid. The US adopted then waived the Graham Act's principal sanctions and waived diesel-deal sanctions through April 2027, splitting the sanctions coalition while the EU adopted 30+ rounds since April 2025.
situation_brief.dynamics: Attrition favors neither side decisively: Russian contract recruitment (~71,000 in Q1 2026 against a ~409,000 annual target) lags losses, while Ukraine's initiative depends on Western aid, intelligence and Starlink/Starshield access. Diplomacy runs through a single US-mediated trilateral channel restarted twice, with Putin bundling goodwill (Iran, fertiliser, detainee release) rather than moving on core terms against Zelensky's standing offer (since November 2024) to freeze the current frontline with US/European guarantees. Termination research finds fighting more often 'simply ceases' than ends by agreement.

scenarios.name: Attrition grinds on
scenarios.narrative: Talks stall over territory and sanctions sequencing and the war continues at reduced but substantial intensity through 2027; prior: most wars of this duration persist past a 2-year window.

scenarios.name: Frozen frontline
scenarios.narrative: A de facto ceasefire freezes the current line without a signed accord as both sides exhaust offensive capacity and the US presses Kyiv; prior: frozen-conflict terminations are common in post-Soviet wars.

scenarios.name: Formal ceasefire signed
scenarios.narrative: The trilateral track produces a signed ceasefire or armistice in force before end-2027, with security guarantees and sanctions relief still unsettled.

scenarios.name: Full-scale war intensifies
scenarios.narrative: Negotiations collapse and Russia re-escalates with a new offensive, returning the war to current or higher intensity.

scenarios.name: Comprehensive peace settlement
scenarios.narrative: A full settlement with territorial terms, security guarantees and sanctions relief enters into force by end-2027; prior: comprehensive settlements within 2 years of talks are rare.

drivers.variable: Trilateral talks convening and level (technical vs ministerial, written text)
drivers.direction: Convening at ministerial level with a circulating text moves toward Formal ceasefire signed — 20%; failure/stall locks in Attrition grinds on — 35%
drivers.why_it_matters: The single US-mediated channel resumed on or after Nov 10, 2026 is the only active path to a signed instrument [S6]

drivers.variable: Russian contract recruitment vs attrition (pace vs ~409,000 annual target)
drivers.direction: Shortfall below ~70% of required pace moves toward Frozen frontline — 25%; a new mobilization decree moves toward Full-scale war intensifies — 15%
drivers.why_it_matters: Q1 2026 intake of ~71,000 was the weakest in three years, ~20% down y/y, against overlapping weekly loss (5,000–8,200) and recruitment (5,500–8,000) ranges [S33][S13]

drivers.variable: Net territorial change on the front
drivers.direction: Continued Russian net losses support Frozen frontline — 25%; renewed gains above the 74 sq mi/month trailing average support Full-scale war intensifies — 15%
drivers.why_it_matters: Russia net-lost ~73 km² since Sept 1, 2026 and ISW judges its Donetsk offensive 'operationally defeated' [S1][S2]

drivers.direction: A sustained month above the May 2026 peak of 8,161 moves toward Full-scale war intensifies — 15%; decline signals (b) or (c)
drivers.why_it_matters: Strike tempo is the operative measure of intensity; September 2026 saw 6,732 Shahed-type UAVs, +30.3% m/m [S3]

drivers.variable: US sanctions posture (diesel waiver lapse vs renewal vs broadening at April 2027 expiry; congressional binding legislation)
drivers.direction: Broadening moves toward Formal ceasefire signed — 20%; lapse or Congress binding waivers over White House objection raises Attrition grinds on — 35%
drivers.why_it_matters: The US waived the Graham Act's principal sanctions and a diesel arrangement runs through April 2027, splitting the coalition [S62][S4][S61]

drivers.variable: Western military aid flows and Starlink/Starshield access
drivers.direction: Aid holding at 2025 pace supports Attrition grinds on — 35%; interruption degrades Ukraine's initiative
drivers.why_it_matters: ISW conditions Ukraine's initiative on US aid, intelligence and Starlink/Starshield access, restored October 15, 2026 [S1][S35][S17]

drivers.variable: EU financing of the €70 billion 2027 gap
drivers.direction: Closing the gap supports Frozen frontline — 25%; shortfall raises Attrition grinds on — 35% and Full-scale war intensifies — 15%
drivers.why_it_matters: The €90 billion EU loan covers about two-thirds of 2026–27 needs and partners' expected €45 billion is slow to arrive [S51][S35]

drivers.variable: Russian fiscal strain (borrowing path, NWF drawdowns, Brent vs the $53/bbl fiscal-rule cutoff)
drivers.direction: Forced monetization or NWF liquid exhaustion would flag fiscal strain and weaken Russia's war sustainment
drivers.why_it_matters: Net borrowing rises 43% to 7.7 trillion roubles in 2027 and state debt reaches 21.7% of GDP, past the ~20% deemed safe [S43][S44]
